title: Empty an upright lobby dustpan into a wastebasket and park it on its mark
instruction: Empty the sweepings (paper ball, bottle cap, folded card, tape core) from the upright lobby dustpan into the wastebasket, then stand the dustpan back on its floor mark with its handle upright.
context: Janitors gather and empty trash (O*NET 37-2011.00, about 2.2 million US jobs). Unlike emptying a small rigid cup in one wrist turn (TK-QBS8FN), this full-size upright dustpan hangs its loaded hopper on a free pivot: it must be tipped by the rear grip recess while the long handle is held over the bin, then set back down so it lands flat and stable.
setup: Floor frame in mm: origin on the floor below the midpoint between the arm bases, x forward, y left. Dustpan: Rubbermaid Commercial FG253100BLA Lobby Pro upright dustpan, 914.4 mm assembled height (maker), black polypropylene hopper 323.9 x 285.8 x 127.0 mm (maker) with a molded rear grip recess and rear wheels, 22 mm vinyl-coated steel handle; the hopper pivots on its rear yoke between a rest stop and a carry stop. Its yoke pivot stands at (340, -180), hopper flat, mouth facing +y, handle leaning about 8 deg rearward on its rest stop, inside a rectangle centred on the same point and made with 14 mm yellow floor tape. The tape centre lines are 400 x 360 mm and the outer edges are 414 x 374 mm. Sweepings on the hopper floor: an empty 3 in kraft shipping-tape core (76.2 mm ID, 82.6 mm OD, 50.8 mm tall, 29 g) standing upright, centre (285, -278); a crumpled sheet of white A4 80 g/m2 copy paper (about 60 mm ball, 5 g), centre (400, -290); a blue polypropylene soda-bottle cap (30 mm across, 12 mm tall, 2 g) lying open side down, centre (400, -220); a green paperboard card folded in half (80 x 50 x 3 mm, 3 g) lying flat, long side along x, centre (290, -200). Wastebasket: Rubbermaid FG295600BLA 28 qt rectangular wastebasket (365 x 260 x 381 mm, LLDPE, 0.74 kg maker), long side along x, centred at (390, 185) inside a 420 x 310 mm white floor-tape outline. A 100 mm black and white floor scale bar lies at (220, 0). Nothing else is on the floor.
scoring: Any direct contact between a robot arm or gripper and any of the four items scores 0. An item earns transfer credit only if it passes forward through the hopper mouth while the hopper floor slopes at least 15 deg downward toward the mouth and the lip midpoint is above the bin opening, then its centre passes downward through the opening within 1 s. Credit is lost if the item leaves the bin. All positive scores require the following at the end: the wastebasket is upright (tilt no more than 10 deg, base no more than 15 mm off the floor); every gripper fingertip stays at least 80 mm from the dustpan, wastebasket and items throughout the last 1 s; and none of the marked points (hopper rear-left base corner, front-right lip corner, grip recess, handle top, two opposite wastebasket corners, two opposite points on each item) moved more than 5 mm in the last 1 s. 1.0 if all four items qualify and end wholly inside the bin inner walls, 50 mm or more below the rim, and the dustpan stays parked on its mark throughout the final 1 s: all four corners of the hopper's base footprint inside the outer edge of the yellow tape rectangle, the base no more than 15 mm above the floor, the hopper tilted no more than 10 deg and the handle within 15 deg of vertical. 0.5 if at least two items qualify and end that way and every other item is wholly within the hopper floor, walls and mouth line; parking on the mark is not needed for 0.5. 0 otherwise, including any item that ends in the bin without qualifying or outside both containers. Possible scores: 0, 0.5, 1.0. Real trial: use synchronized side and overhead video to verify the hopper tilt, each item's two crossings, arm-to-item contact, release and final stillness. Check the overhead video across the final second and retain a final photo showing that all four hopper base corners are inside the tape's outer edge, and a ruler and phone level for the other placement checks and angles.
reset_notes: Before the first trial, tape the dustpan rectangle and the wastebasket outline on the floor and pencil the four item centres on the hopper floor. Each reset: stand the dustpan with its yoke pivot on the rectangle centre, hopper flat, mouth facing +y, handle on its rest stop; place the same four items on their marks as in the setup (core upright, cap open side down, card flat with its long side along x, paper ball re-crumpled to about 60 mm); place the wastebasket in its outline, long side along x. Replace the core if it is crushed or out of round, and the paper ball or card if torn.
fidelity: The hopper pivots on a passive yoke with modelled rest (+8 deg) and carry (-90 deg) stops and no spring. Masses are estimates: dustpan 0.84 kg (maker packaged weight), core 29 g, paper 5 g, cap 2 g, card 3 g. Hopper, recess and wastebasket are boxes; the core is a 12-segment ring, the crumpled paper a rigid 42-vertex convex hull, the card a rigid box, the cap a solid cylinder (the real cap is hollow). Release distance and stillness are simulated checks of the stated thresholds.
